description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/8937501?from=youtube_share 
Here's another tune pertaining to the early automobile. In 1899 the automobile was definitely not the major mode of transportation but more of a novelty that was initially greeted with some skepticism ("Get a horse!" was commonly heard in those days). They were usually open carriages and quite primitive by today's standards. But here's a pleasant piece that takes us for an automobile spin written in a polite gavotte, or dance, style. description:

Eleanora Beauchamp Smith (1892-1981) was born and died in Kentucky. This brilliant folk rag is her only known published composition. It was included in the Nora Hulse CD "60 Years of Ragtime". According to Geoff Grainger, she probably trained as a concert pianist in Cincinnati, taught piano and voice and gave recitals. title: File:"Marching Through Georgia" by Henry C. Work – sung by Harlan & Stanley (1904).ogg
description:
A 1904 phonographic recording of Henry C. Work's "Marching Through Georgia", sung by Byron G. Harlan (1861–1936) and Frank C. Stanley (1868–1910). The song, penned following General Sherman's March to the Sea in 1865, sold over 500,000 copies and was a cornerstone of any Unionist reunion. 
It was picked up by Edison's record label at the height of its popularity. The popular music duo Harlan & Stanley, one of the most renowned of their time, performed the song multiple times at the turn of the 20th century. title: File:"Pretty Pol'" (1927), by Little Jack Little.oga
description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/25311208?from=youtube_share 
A very well done score that captures the essence of what Novelty Piano sounded like in 1927 by the well-known singer and songwriter Little Jack Little (1899-1956). It appears to be his only novelty piece. He was born in England, came to the United States at age 9. He was an outstanding singer as well as a musician and bandleader, was frequently heard on radio and was a prolific recording artist during the 1930s. As a songwriter his best known song was "In a Shanty in Old Shanty Town".

description:
If this rag doesn't tickle your shoe, nothing will. A one-of-a-kind rag from Los Angeles, which in 1911 had only about one tenth of the number of residents the city does now and wasn't on the main map in regards to ragtime. Not surprisingly there's a story attached regarding the composer, Wilbur Watkins Campbell (1889-1951), who was a lifelong resident of this same city.
This is the only known rag attributed to Campbell, who in addition to composing was a pianist and a civil engineer. For a time (1913-1918) he was married to socialite Marian dePaux Beveridge, daughter of Daeida Hartell Wilcox

Bess Rudisill was a professional pianist, organist and composer originally from Missouri. She was a local teenage sensation on the piano and was publishing her works from age 17, including this one in 1901 (re-issued in 1902 by S. Simon in St. Louis). This one is a "characteristic two-step", more like a march, and is quite good. She published about 10 compositions altogether.

title: File:'A quien le importa', himno del World Pride Madrid 2017.webm
description:
Desde WorldPride Madrid han decidido que qué mejor himno para el WorldPride Madrid 2017 que la canción que compusieron Carlos Berlanga y Nacho Canut en 1986, 'A quién le importa', convertida en un referente de la reivindicación de los derechos LGTB desde entonces.
La nueva versión, realizada por el habitual productor de Fangoria, Juan Sueiro, además de Alaska y Nacho Canut, ha contado con la participación de (por orden de aparición) Nancys Rubias, Baccara, Chenoa, Innocence, Ruth Lorenzo, Vicky Larraz (Olé Olé), Marta Sánchez, La Prohibida, Javiera Mena, Rosa López, Soraya Arnelas, La Terremot

Converted from MP3 to Ogg Vorbis with a slight trim of the beginning and end by Major Bloodnok.
The discography of Joplin's work on 78 rpm records compiled by David A Jasen in "Complete works of Scott Joplin" indicates this is the third known recording of the Maple Leaf Rag. E

Bach was confronted with this 'Reformation Day' in Leipzig. He came up with a festive instrumentation in 'Gott der Herr ist Sonn und Schild': in addition to the strings and continuo, it also involved two oboes, two horns and timpani. title: File:31st Street Blues - Henderson's Club Alabam' Orchestra (1923).mp3
description:
All of the following info is from the original YouTube description:
The first record to give label credit to Fletcher Henderson's Club Alabam' Orchestra, named after the basement club where the Henderson band took up residence in November of 1923. Located on W. 44th Street, it had been operated as a speakeasy known as the Little Club that was raided by the Feds in April 1923 and closed down as a result.
31st Street Blues was so named from a popular street in Chicago. Henderson later recorded it with Clara Smith and again with Josie Miles. I'm a big fan of the early Henderson band!

title: File:A Chinese Salmagundi by Noel Lehsif (1902).opus
description:
Salmagundi is a salad that can be made of a wide assortment of ingredients in addition to vegetables. Figuratively it could mean "any miscellaneous mixture or assortment." So here you have a Chinese Salmagundi, another example of a wonderfully eccentric folk rag from the early days of ragtime. It's also a rare rag that's a bit of a mystery, the cover is missing and the only clue is that it was published by the Lehsif Music Pub. Co. in 1902.
Musescore researcher Erlingl finds no evidence of a person named Noel Lehsif who actually existed beyond this composition. But in a brilliant bit of detect
credit:
YouTube: A Chinese Salmagundi by Noel Lehsif (1902) – View/save archived versions on archive.org

I have posted the copy of the original score at this link: https://mega.nz/file/WERAgSKB#dxWU-5MXE2EOzR2qvRZXIqB5gw2pF9bspevAhchp5eU

title: File:After The Ball (1892).opus
description:
This song, with music and lyrics by Charles K. Harris, was the most successful song of its era, selling over two million copies of sheet music in 1892. Its total sheet music sales exceed five million copies, making it the best seller in Tin Pan Alley's history.
It embodied the style of early Origipop songs which often had several verses, with each verse possessing 6 or 7 lines and being used to tell long, detailed stories.

description:
Brandenburg Concerto No. 5 (in D major, BWV 1050)

As the opening movement of the Brandenburg Concerto Number Five in D major unfolds, the harpsichord seems at first willing to play a subservient role as part of the continuo. But as time goes on it becomes more and more assertive until finally it bursts forth into an astonishing cadenza of tremendous difficulty. Violin and flute share the solo spot at the beginning. but once the cadenza begins, they are cast completely into the shade. At the opening of the cadenza, we are listening to the dying strains from the keyboard as mere continuo accomp

He was an early ragtimer, both in composition and performing, and led ragtime bands based in Detroit, Michigan becoming a respected presence in the Detroit music scene. He was mainly involved in performing but also wrote the occasional waltz, march or ragtime-related score like this one. He tragically died at age 39 in a trolley car accident in Detroit. This march two-step was published by Jerome H. Remick in Detroit and New York in 1905. This is a reproduction of the origi

title: File:Brandenburg Concerto No. 4 in G, Movement I (Allegro), BWV 1049 (ISRC USUAN1100303).mp3
description:
Brandenburg Concerto No. 4 in G, Movement I (Allegro), BWV 1049
Bach. Violin, 2 Flutes (standard C Flute in this case), a mess of strings, and harpsichord. The primary violin is obviously sampled in a few of the faster passages, but the sweet tone shines through nicely on the slower notes. This is my first attempt at a Brandenburg... I suspect I'll revisit this one after I get a few more recorded. Still, it is probably the best free and digital recording available.
artist: Original Composition: Bach ; Brandenburg Concerto No. 4 in G, Movement I (Allegro), BWV 1049; Arrangment and performance:  Kevin MacLeod

title: File:Chantecler by Jeanne Delmar (1910).opus
description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/8213645?from=youtube_share 
Chantecler was the name of a French play which premiered in 1910 where the main character was a rooster. It is also the name of this robust Canadian march two-step, self-published in Montreal in 1910 by an otherwise unknown composer. Stick around for the Trio, it'll get you hopping. Researcher JohnJ1995 informs me that the play also inspired a number of other compositions from 1910, some using the English adapted title "Chanticleer".

Score #140 in my ongoing current series "Women Ragt

title: File:Children's corner of Meng.ogg
description: Jason, why did you submit this edition, is it yours? No, no, this sound was made by myself, but the content was from 'my kid's' learning progress' of Sir Debussy's 'Doctorial' in Children's corner. You knew, Sir Debussy has his own daughter; but till this year - my age of 30 year's old, I haven't gotten any. Therefore, in this period, I saw my students as my kids. Oh, it was by accident that I had recorded one piece of a little girl's exercises in classroom (around 13 or 14). Her name was Xue Meng, Hu and her 'little doctor edition' was Live-voicing in this place.File:Meng Meng with Christmas
name: Children's corner of Meng
categories: Category:Audio files of music by Claude Debussy

title: File:Ching Chong - Piano Roll.opus
description: In this video, I'm playing "Ching Chong" (Chinese One-step) on my 1914 Autopiano Player Piano.  This is antique QRS Autograph roll 100578 with music by Lee S. Roberts and played by Ted Baxter & Max Kortlander.  I'm intrigued by this roll after seeing a number of other Youtube videos of it posted, but under a different QRS roll number - and with words.  I didn't realize this song had words until seeing those other videos, since this roll doesn't have any.

description:
Claude Debussy's: The Cave (« La Grotte »), n. 2 of the Three Songs of France (« Trois Chansons de France », 1904), a cycle of French melodies based on poems by Charles of Orléans and Tristan L'Hermite. The Cave, with a title given by the composer and reminiscent of the 3rd scene of Act 2 of his opera Pelléas and Mélisande (« Pelléas et Mélisande »), is a musical setting of the ode The Walk of the Two Lovers (« Le Promenoir des deux amants »), by L'Hermite.

title: File:Claude Debussy, Images - 06 Poissons d'or (Marcelle Meyer, 1957).flac
description:
Marcelle Meyer's interpretation of Golden Fish (« Poissons d'or »), a piece dedicated to the pianist Ricardo Viñes and which is number 3 of the second series of the piano suite Images by Claude Debussy. The piece is inspired by a Japanese panel lacquered in black and inlaid with mother-of-pearl and gold, which depicted two goldfish, with golden reflections, in a stylised river; the artefact was located in the composer's studio and is now exhibited in the Claude Debussy Museum in Saint-Germain-en-Laye, the musician's birthplace.

title: File:Clementi Sonatina Opus 36 Number 5 Movement I Presto.oga
description:
Jason, if getting back to your childhood, whose series of sonatina did you most prefer to pick up again? Muzio Clementi's Op. 36, No. 5 - yes, I have chosen it with 3 paragraphs. But dear, why? why not the No.1...or others'? Yes, it was also good for a kid's heart... But, this one was my preference that I thought it was 'near kids' minds, near heaven, and angels' cries'.

name: Clementi Sonatina Opus 36 Number 5 Movement I Presto
categories: Category:Audio files of music by Muzio Clementi

title: File:Clementi Sonatina Opus 36 Number 5 Movement II Air Suisse.oga
description:
It was the second paragraph of Clementi's Op. 36 No. 5 following Jason' CO36N5I in this series. I can remember: in my manuscript, beside its title, it was written 'Swiss Folk Song'. In Jason's curious eyes of his age, the imagination was mapping out, to a peaceful town-liked country under the background of a snow mountain; and a lake was there... Then, people were freely boating and enjoying their holiday time under a sunset landscape...

description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/7408580?from=youtube_share 
Definitely a gem of a rag. Labelled as a novelette and an intermezzo, it's just a really fine rag. Nellie Stokes lived in Detroit where she was employed by the publisher Jerome H. Remick, and took the opportunity to publish seven scores with them until her unfortunate death in 1914 following the birth of her second child. This was one of her last pieces and is, in my opinion, the best one of all. Published in 1909 by Jerome H. Remick in Detroit and New York.

description:
Dreams Become Real
Beautiful dreamy piece that confuses times and spaces. You really just need to take a moment and listen to this one - because it is really cool. How cool? You should probably find out! There are a lot of extra synth things going on in it that are hidden in and amongst the piano, like one of those hidden picture books with 45 paperclips, but you can only ever see 7 of them. 
This music has a unique and timeless ambience. Like browsing ancient wiki pages last edited over a decade ago, as indicated at the page bottom in MediaWiki, but that editor perhaps looked at an earlier it
name: Dreams Become Real (ISRC USUAN1500027)

title: File:Edison cylinder Lost Chord.ogg
description:
An Edison "Perfected" Phonograph cylinder recording of The Lost Chord (composed 1877) by Arthur Sullivan (1842-1900), played on piano and cornet.  One of the earliest surviving recordings of music; was played at the press conference that introduced the phonograph to London on August 14 1888. 
Cuts off slightly before the ending of the song.  The recorded version is somewhat abridged (a middle section has been cut, possibly due to time constraints).  Overall a well-preserved example of wax cylinder recording technology.


Length: 2:07
artist: Recorded by George Gouraud, performers unknown.
name: Edison cylinder Lost Chord

Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/14153062?from=youtube_share 
This interesting rag, with its unusual AABCCBAA format, seems to have been popular judging by the variety of sources online who have the original sheet music listed. Plus it's still being played today by pianists and small orchestras. Of Tad Fischer nothing is known and it's safe to say this was his only rag. Published by O.K. Houck in Memphis, Tennessee in 1912.

description:
"Io non ho che una povera stanzetta" from act 2 of Ruggero Leoncavallos opera La bohème (1897), sung by Enrico Caruso in 1911.
It is probably best to make this explicit: This is NOT from Puccini's La bohème. Ruggiero Leoncavallo, Puccini's contemporary, also made an opera based on the same stories, with the same name. While Puccini's version proved wildly popular, Leoncavallo's faded into obscurity.


This is Matrix # C-11276 recorded 26 November 1911 (details)
artist:
Sung by Enrico Caruso (1873–1921)
Composed and librettoed by Ruggiero Leoncavallo (1857–1919)

title: File:Everybody's Rag by Dan Goldsmith and Robert D. Sharp (1909).opus
description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/6987035?from=youtube_share 
"It Gets You Going". Unique rag by Canadian Dan Goldsmith, co-authored by his Denver, Colorado publisher Robert D. Sharp in 1909, the first of the three that he wrote. Goldsmith was from Winnipeg, Manitoba, a city colder than any city in the United States outside of Alaska. Perhaps that explains the energetic nature of this composition, perhaps they're just trying to get warm!

Original score source was IMSLP.org at this link:
https://ks.imslp.info/files/imglnks/usimg/5/58/IMSLP672065-
artist: Dan Goldsmith (d. 1920) and Robert D. Sharp

title: File:Friedrich Wilhelm Nietzsche - Hoch tut euch auf.oga
description: Lift Up Your Heads, for four-part choir a capella. Motet. Written December 1858 for his family. Since the original version consists of separate parts, which do not always fit together, was created a work for chorus a cappella. As in many later works, Nietzsche does not finish this work in the way it began. The transition from G major to E major gives special emphasis to the festive character of the text (Psalm 24, 7) that Nietzsche found in a German translation of Handel's The Messiah (№ 33).
name: Friedrich Wilhelm Nietzsche - Hoch tut euch auf

title: File:Glad Rags by Anna Hughes Carpenter (1907).opus
description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/8070798?from=youtube_share 
I would describe this composition as an amalgamation of various cakewalkey segments into one interesting score, hence the title "Glad Rags". Written by an otherwise unknown composer, it was published in Cincinnati, Ohio in 1907 by George Jaberg Music Co.

Score #121 in my current ongoing series "Women Ragtime Composers" featuring interesting scores all written by ragtime-era women. No end in sight to this series.
Original score source was from the Charles Templeton Sheet Music Collecti

title: File:Great Crush Collision March by Scott Joplin (1896).opus
description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/10251316?from=youtube_share 
In 1896 an agent of the Missouri, Kansas and Texas Railway named George Crush arranged to have a spectacular event occur in a deserted valley north of Waco, Texas. title: File:Hardwood Rag by Jack Sight (1909).opus
description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/12999421?from=youtube_share 
Here's a really good rag from Kansas City by a one-off composer. Published by J.W. Jenkins in Kansas City, Missouri in 1909.

Original score source was from Indiana University at this link:
https://fedora.dlib.indiana.edu/fedora/get/iudl:275420/OVERVIEW
This is a reproduction of the original score. I changed the second voice at measure 53 so the note durations of the G make sense.
Thank you to Mitchy for the great suggestion.
My YouTube channel is here:
https://www.youtube.com/@compuk

title: File:Hunkatin by Sol P. Levy (1918).opus
description: Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/13237120?from=youtube_share "Hunkatin" appears to be a derogatory term for automobile ("hunk of tin"). So why is it the title of this very smooth, well-done dance number? In the tradition of "Too Much Mustard" it's just a funny way of getting some attention. And it apparently worked, as "Hunkatin" was recorded by orchestras on disk in the day and is still performed today. Original score source was from the Charles Templeton Sheet Music Collection at Mississippi State University at this link: https://scholarsjunct
artist: Sol Paul Levy's career was gaining momentum as a composer and publisher in the years around World War 1, but he died in 1920 at age 38. "Hunkatin" was published by Belwin, Inc. in New York City in 191
credit: YouTube: Hunkatin by Sol P. Levy (1918) – View/save archived versions on archive.org

"March  Two-Step". Julia Lee Niebergall was a professional pianist and music teacher from Indiana who published several pieces, including the three rags I will feature here. Described as fiery and independent, it's claimed she was the first woman in Indianapolis to own an automobile. "Hoosier" is the official term for anyone who comes from Indiana (no one knows where the word actually derived from). title: File:Hop To It by George A. Hardwick (1920).opus
description: "One Step or Fox Trot". I guess by 1920 rags were no longer in fashion, which explains why this well-crafted folk rag was labelled as a fox trot, which were in vogue at the time. And it's a rare one, self-published by George A. Hardwick from Glenwood Springs, Colorado, which is still a lovely resort town. With some help from Musescore researcher Erlingl we've been able to determine that George Albert Hardwick was born in Missouri in 1873, the youngest in a very large family, to farmer John Hardwick and his wife Sarah. title: File:IMSLP365260-PMLP02284-Mazurka gis-moll Op 33 Nr 1.ogg
description: Mazurka in G-sharp minor, Op. 33, No. 1, the opening mazurka of the set, has a tempo marking of Lento. This mazurka has an emotional melody, accompanied in the left hand with a waltz pattern. The mood changes many times throughout the piece, and to good effect. This intimate piece is occasionally considered less complicated than many of Chopin's other mazurkas.

categories: Category:Audio files of mazurkas by Frédéric Chopin

title: File:IMSLP365261-PMLP02284-Mazurka D-Dur Op 33 Nr 2.ogg
description:
Mazurka in D major, Op. 33, No. 2, the second piece of the collection, is one of the most popular mazurkas. It has a fast tempo and strong irregular accents.
The piece begins with the happy and joyful main theme, decorated with ornaments. After a second theme is introduced, the main theme is repeated for a second time. The mazurka concludes with a separate coda section that introduces a new theme, this concludes with a melody ascending high into the upper register.

title: File:IMSLP365263-PMLP02284-Mazurka h-moll Op 33 Nr 4.ogg
description:
Mazurka in B minor, Op. 33, No. 4, the final mazurka of the set, is one of the longest mazurkas at nearly 5 minutes in length. The piece is written in an ABABCA structure, similar to a rondo form.
The piece begins with a captivating main melody, decorated with grace notes and trills. This melody is repeated a total of eight times throughout the piece; between it, different melodies appear, but the main melody always returns. A B♭ major section follows the theme, which is the B section. The C section is in B major, which is the parallel key to B minor.

title: File:IMSLP365275-PMLP02279-Mazurka As- Dur Op 59 Nr 2.ogg
description:
Mazurka in A-flat major is the second and shortest of the Op. 59 mazurkas, with a typical performance lasting around 2 and a half minutes.
The piece begins with a memorable main theme that Chopin varies from time to time to maintain the piece's interest. The trio section of the piece is very similar to the main theme, providing little contrast. The piece concludes with an interesting coda, full of accidentals and chromatic harmonies and finishing on a tonic chord, repeated 4 times.
name: IMSLP365275-PMLP02279-Mazurka As- Dur Op 59 Nr 2
categories: Category:Audio files of mazurkas by Frédéric Chopin

title: File:IMSLP365276-PMLP02279-Mazurka fis-moll Op 59 Nr 3.ogg
description:
Mazurka in F-sharp minor, the final piece of the set, is referring to an oberek, a national Polish dance much faster than a mazurka. The piece begins with a memorable and powerful melody, the second theme is somewhat more joyful than the first. The left hand accompaniment of the piece experiments with descending chromatic harmonies, although this does not affect the melody which remains defined throughout the piece.
An autograph manuscript housed at the Morgan Library & Museum in New York contains a complete draft of this Mazurka written in the key of G minor, dedicated to Ferdinand Hiller
name: IMSLP365276-PMLP02279-Mazurka fis-moll Op 59 Nr 3
categories: Category:Audio files of mazurkas by Frédéric Chopin

title: File:Jazzapation by Edward B. Claypoole (1920).opus
description:
Original listing and sheet music here: /user/36482158/scores/7077622?from=youtube_share 
A novelty fox trot from composer Edward B. Claypoole (1883-1952), a great writer of novelties. His first published works were from age 15. His day job for decades was that of a law clerk for the court system of Baltimore, Maryland, but he still found time to write and perform music, and was in demand for his piano performances.

Original score source was from York University at this link:
https://yorkspace.library.yorku.ca/xmlui/bitstream/handle/10315/14561/JAC000955.pdf?sequence=2&isAllowed=y

description:
BWV 997 - Lute Suite No. 2 in C minor - I Prelude

An instrument maker Hildebrand was commissioned by JS Bach to build a keyboard lute (Lautenwerk) of Bach's design. He subsequently wrote 3 compositions believed to be for that instrument: S996, S997 and S998. The instrument on this recording (built by A. Goldstein) is believed to be the first keyboard lute after 200 years. It was built in 1978.

The harpsichord is copied from a one manual instrument built by Hans Moerman in Antwerp (1584). It was restored by Frank Hubbard in Boston (1963). title: File:John Philip Sousa's "The Glory of the Yankee Navy" performed by the United States Marine Band in June 1978.oga
description: "The Glory of the Yankee Navy" performed by the USMC Band. March, “The Glory of the Yankee Navy" (1909) - The musical comedy The Yankee Girl was in need of a spirited march, so Sousa was prevailed upon to provide one. The march, one of Sousa’s most interesting musically, was dedicated to the star of the show, Blanche Ring. Lyrics  were provided by Kenneth S. Clark. The title underwent a process of evolution. The earliest known manuscript was labeled “Uncle Sam’s Navy.” Prior to the opening, newspapers referred to the march as “The Honor of the Yankee Navy.”
credit: YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bjGD588htyc – View/save archived versions on archive.org

description:
Finale of Louis Vierne's "Organ Symphony No. 1" (1898-1899), performed by Marc Giacone on the organ of Monaco Cathedral in 2004.

The symphony is dedicated to Alexandre Guilmant, whose assistant at the Conservatory was Vierne.


See also "List of organ symphonies", "Organ Symphonies (Vierne)", "List of organ symphonies: Louis Vierne (1870–1937): Organ Symphony No. 1, Op. 14 (1895)" and "Louis Vierne: Music: Final Movement of Organ Symphony No. 1 in D minor, op. 14".

title: File:Maltese Cross Brand by Wilfred G. Astle (1905).opus
description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/6983867?from=youtube_share 
What's fascinating about this composition is that it starts out as a standard march but at the final strain (measure 76 onwards) it turns into a syncopated rag, as if to demonstrate how adding syncopation results in ragtime. Self-published by Wilfred G. Astle in Toronto, Ontario, Canada in 1905.

This is the original score replicated. The original can be found via ragtimepiano.ca at this link:
https://www.nlc-bnc.ca/obj/m5/f2/csm629.pdf
Link to Canadian Scores playlist:
https://www.you
credit: YouTube: Maltese Cross Brand by Wilfred G. Astle (1905) – View/save archived versions on archive.org

title: File:Moonlight Sonata (Sharp c minor Sonata) 2nd Movement Beethoven JMC,Han.ogg
description:
As the caption's introduction, There are two editions of Moonlight Sonata (2nd Movement), regarding with which I cannot decided to keep or give up one, besides the other. They were all after a careful notation-reading, but, the first one was formal and more carefully; while, the other, a little bit of rough, but 'emotional reaches' onto a higher musicality, in my mind. If classroom-teaching, I would choose the first one, while, outside performing, the second one.

description:
As the caption's introduction, There are two editions of Moonlight Sonata (2nd Movement), regarding with which I cannot decided to keep or give up one, besides the other. They were all after a careful notation-reading, but, the first one was formal and more carefully; while, the other, a little bit of rough, but 'emotional reaches' onto a higher musicality, in my mind. If classroom-teaching, I would choose the first one, while, outside performing, the second one better. 
You may ask me: Jason, how could you understand the musicality of this movement? And, what type was it in your imagination?

title: File:My Pal - Piano Roll.opus
description: In this video, I'm playing "My Pal" on my 1914 Autopiano Player Piano.  This is antique Connorized roll 11017 and played by S. A. Perry.  I picked up this roll in a flea market some years ago, and was intrigued by the "U-Play Banjo-Mand-Uke-ETC" marking on the label.  While not my favorite song per se, I do find the instructions at the beginning of the roll and chord markings in the left margin to be really interesting and unique.  It's fun to imagine the roll being played and someone attempting to play along with it that way!

description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/7714814?from=youtube_share 
Fun rag doing a little bit of parodying, probably to rouse some patriotism during World War 1. Some of it is a bit abstract, but I think I hear a little bit of Yankee Doodle, a lot of Dixie and a brief blast of the Star Spangled Banner. Written by piano teacher Marcella Henry who was well involved with Axel Christensen's piano teaching schools in Chicago. This is the second of the five rags she wrote, all of which are being featured in this series plus a waltz. This score only appeared

title: File:Omar Rabbi Elozor original.ogg
description:
Unedited version of "Omar Rabbi Elozor" (Modern transliteration: Amar Rabi Elazar - "Said Rabbi Eliezar", performed by Cantor Meyer Kanewsky and his choir in 1919 for Edison Records. This is Edison Diamond Disc 75001-R The text begins, roughly, "Said Rabbi Elazar, quoting Rabbi Chaninah, Scholars increase the levels of peace in the world." In Judaism, this passage is commonly used in the Sunday Morning Service.
Text
The text is basically the last passage from Tractate Berakhot, from the Talmud, with a few repeats.
credit: Library of Congress, Edison Records collection
name: Omar Rabbi Elozor original

title: File:Piece for Panharmonikon - Wellingtons Sieg, oder die Schlacht bei Vittoria (Wellington’s Victory, or the Battle of Vittoria).ogg
description: Enthused, Beethoven (according to Moscheles, upon Maelzel's suggestion) wrote the composition The Battle of Vittoria in 1813, commemorating the victory of the Duke of Wellington over the French forces, for this new instrument. Beethoven stated that he had already conceived the idea of a battle, which was not practicable on the Panharmonikon. However, Moscheles is probably more accurate, since the front page of the Panharmonikon score states, in Beethoven's hand, that it was "written for Hr. Maelzel by Ludwig van Beethoven."
artist:
Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827), the composer

Wladyslav Kozjin (b.1993), the musician (transcriber from Beethoven's original partiture)

title: File:Prelude S. PROKOFIEV OP. 12 NO. 7 Performer Jason M. C., Han.ogg
description:
In the worlds-list of the  memorized piano tunes from my nature , there was a space for  S. PROKOFIEV. It's not a huge one but a small river nearby Heaven - OP. 12 NO. 7 Prelude. 
To be honest, I didn't know too much about this melody and its composer. Just when reading its notation, I felt very excited - like in a situation I was still a childhood boy happily playing waves, skillfully making all kinds of swimming-postures, exaggeratedly running after big fishes, yellow ducks,  and marine animals... 
I liked the atmosphere right hand created in A part of ABA structure very much, which gave you
name: Prelude S. PROKOFIEV OP. 12 NO. 7 Performer Jason M. C., Han
categories: Category:Audio files of music by Sergei Prokofiev

title: File:Primary Bach No. 16 March, Player JMC, Han.ogg
description:
Back to my Earlier Years, the teaching book 'Primary Level Bach' used to be one of the beginning several ones I touched, coming me closed to my life-long good peer - Piano... 
On these COVID-19 days, opening new era exam-collection book made me see No.16 piece there, for primary level... Memory-door opened:
In my little eyes those days, Bach was very hard, but world in Bach Music was quite in 'Good manners', peaceful (comfortable when getting one) and rational... like watching a magnificent palace or church, and a well-behaved dance in.
I can remember my hands in those days weren't so
skillful
name: Primary Bach No. 16 March, Player JMC, Han
categories: Category:Audio files of Baroque period classical music
Category:Audio files of music by Johann Sebastian Bach

title: File:Queen Raglan by A.E. Henrich (1902).opus
description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/40436745?from=youtube_share 
"Cake Walk Two Step". Spelled "Queen Raglan" on the cover and "Queen Raglin" on the sheet music. A well-written cakewalk rag by Arthur E. Henrich (1878-1954). Henrich was a musician and professional piano tuner who wrote four pieces, including this cakewalk published in Nashville, Tennessee by H.A. French in 1902, his final score. He was originally from New Vernon, Indiana and traveled a lot, later settling in California. He lived to be 75 years old, dying in Indiana in 1954.

Origina

description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/14333248?from=youtube_share 
Harry Thomas (1890-1941) was born Reginald Thomas Broughton in Bristol, England and immigrated to Canada at age 19, settling in Montreal. He was an excellent self-taught pianist and worked with established Montreal pianist-composer Willie Eckstein. In 1916 he went to Chicago and New York to cut piano rolls and make recordings, including Eckstein's "Delirious Rag". This appears to be his only published rag, which was published by Delmar Music in Montreal in 1909.

title: File:Red Peppers by Imogene Giles (1907).opus
description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/7240050?from=youtube_share 
Another classic ragtime piece, so well written, that needs to be saved from the jaws of obscurity. Imogene (Daisy) Giles was from Quincy, Illinois where she was established as a pianist and music teacher and helped run her husband's music business, which also published this rag in 1907. It's her only known rag and leaves one wondering what she could have done if she had been able to publish more of these.

Score #34 in my current set series "Women Ragtime Composers". The others uploade
credit: YouTube: Red Peppers by Imogene Giles (1907) – View/save archived versions on archive.org
name: Red Peppers by Imogene Giles (1907)

title: File:Rose Leaf Rag by Scott Joplin (1907).opus
description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/9217260?from=youtube_share 
Scott Joplin produced some of his most "classical" rags starting in 1907, and this one is no exception. Well-done and well-acclaimed, it has an uplifting concluding D section which is marked giocoso, meaning "in a lively and playful manner". By this time Joplin made his way to New York City and had this rag published with Boston publisher Joseph M. Daly in 1907.

Original score source was from the Charles Templeton Sheet Music Collection at Mississippi State University at this link:

title: File:Rudy Vallee's 1928 Victor Audition - Georgie Porgie - Cliff Burwell (Piano).opus
description:
Here is a true one of a kind Rudy Vallee rarity, Rudy's audition for Victor from June 4, 1928!  Vallee brought Georgie Porgie back to the US upon his return to Yale in 1925 and it was a standard tune of his band, The Yale Collegians and later The Connecticut Yankees.  
By 1928, he had started to make a name for himself through his records for Diva/Velvet Tone/Harmony labels and Victor was interested in signing him to an exclusive contract. It's one Sinfonia - 3 parts Invention of my most favorites since childhood LIVE-recorded (Fine Mobile-recorder)in my piano room. Now, no other students but myself to do so, because of COVID-19 Defence. 
This piece of Bach's 15 Sinfonias is much closed to my nature. I can remember the time of my childhood firstly hearing it, but I didn't have chance to touch it. Now, I can have time. Some books said the musicality of it is a little bit sad, or to say, sorrow, like to go through a tragedic hero's heart-road. However, I through it's like to sing a small carol in a small church, praying for people

description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/11878282?from=youtube_share 
Archie Scheu's most enduring rag in terms of popularity of the four he wrote, and why not as it is an excellent and very smooth rag. It was recorded by John Philip Sousa's band with Arthur Pryor in 1908 and is still popular today. Published by A.W. Scheu Music Publishing Co. in Cincinnati, Ohio in 1907.

Original score source was from the Charles Templeton Sheet Music Collection at Mississippi State University at this link:
https://scholarsjunction.msstate.edu/cht-sheet-music/12878/

title: File:Snowball by Nellie M. Stokes (1906).opus
description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/7572221?from=youtube_share 
"Ragtime March". Perhaps the raggiest of her five rag/march compositions, this is the fifth of all five of them in this series by the talented Nellie Stokes. Published by her employer Jerome H. Remick in Detroit and New York in 1906. Definitely in need of more recognition, her scores have been a highlight of this current series "Women Ragtime Composers". Score #68 in this series 

Filed in my new set "Nellie Stokes" where all five march/rags can be found at this link:
https://musescore

National Park Seminary was a young ladies' finishing school in Montgomery County, Maryland, near Washington DC, a place where wealthy families would send their daughters for some further education beyond high school. It had a number of sororities including the Theta Sigma Rho, where this surprisingly fine rag appears to have originated by an otherwise unknown composer. Published by the Thompson Music Co. in Chicago and New York in 1909. This title also appeared in the Nora Hulse CD "60

title: File:Sue by Fred S. Stone (1902).opus
description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/6985120?from=youtube_share 
Fred S. Stone was born in Ontario to African-American parents originally from Georgia. He grew up in southern Ontario and later became a dual US-Canadian citizen after establishing himself in the Detroit music scene. He continued to perform in Canada also during his working life. He became an important band leader whose band was a very early promoter of ragtime, back as early as the late 1890s. He unfortunately died in 1912 at age 39 in a trolley car accident in Detroit. title: File:Sure, Ma's Version of 'Turkish March' in piano classroom for piano education.ogg
description:
Jason, is this 'sound imagery' yours version? 
No, I am only a piano-classroom recorder for my student Sure, Ma's 'Turkish March' in his childhood. After getting his permission, I hope, in 'Children's corner' of Wikiversity and for the educational purpose, it can be known by more people through wiki-family online.
Sure, Ma is a total pronunciation-translation from this boy's Chinese name. I think it's very interesting: indeed, the meaning of his name is - Ma family's boy born in North Face. But, when you hear the pronunciation from Chinese into English, you will easily find a word 'Sure' to st

title: File:Telemann - Methodical Sonatas - 1. Gmin.ogg
description:
Felix Skowronek plays these sonatas on a wooden flute. Each sonata is played with a head-joint made of different woods, These woods are 1. Orange Rosewood; 2. Mexican Rosewood; 3. African Blackwood (Grenadilla); 4. Brazilian Redwood; 5 Black Ironbox; and 6. Gidgee. 

The first 4 of these were made by the Flutemaker's Guild, London; the last 2, by Skowronek. The first 3 sonatas used an Italian styled harpsichord, while the last 3 used a Flemish styled instrument. Realizations of the figured bass were done by Martha Goldstein.
credit: The Al Goldstein collection in the Pandora Music repository at ibiblio.org.
name: Telemann - Methodical Sonatas - 1. Gmin
categories: Category:Audio files of classical music by Felix Skowronek

title: File:That Old Gang of Mine - Billy Murray, Ed Smalle.flac
description:
"That Old Gang of Mine" is a 1923 popular song composed by Ray Henderson with lyrics by Billy Rose and Mort Dixon, and published by Irving Berlin, Inc. It was introduced in the Ziegfeld Follies of 1923 by the vaudeville duo Van and Schenck.[1] The song became a million-seller.[2]


The song was recorded by many artists in 1923. On June 5, Billy Murray and Ed Smalle recorded the most popular version of "That Old Gang of Mine" (Victor 19095), which went to #1 on US charts.[3]

title: File:That Everlasting Rag by William Held (1911).opus
description:
Will Held (1888-1925) was a Philadelphia musician and music teacher who composed in a variety of genres. He wrote three rags, this one and "Fire Cracker Rag" both in 1911 plus "Chromatic Rag" his best-known work in 1916 which has become an enduring classic. He also married in 1916. HIs life and career were cut short as he died from natural causes in 1925 at the age of 36.
"That Everlasting Rag" was published by Chas. E. Roat Music Co. in Battle Creek, Michigan in 1911. Original score source was from the Charles Templeton Sheet Music Collection at Mississippi State University at this link:
http

name: That Everlasting Rag by William Held (1911)

title: File:The Crane Dance by Max Almen (1904).opus
description: This is one of those rare and overlooked rags that deserves more attention. It starts as a folksy rag but turns into a sort of ragtime extravaganza before it's over, an interesting rag from the earlier days of ragtime. Of the composer we can find no definite details other than he wrote this one rag, which was published by Pioneer Music Publishing Co. in Chicago in 1904. Many thanks to Mitchy for finding this rare rag, which comes from the collection of the late Frank Himpsl posted on the Pianophilia site. This is a reproduction of the original score.
credit:
YouTube: The Crane Dance by Max Almen (1904) – View/save archived versions on archive.org

title: File:The Mikado (1917, Byng-Wood).mp3
description:
A complete recording of The Mikado from 1917.
Byng conducts all numbers except "As someday it may happen," which is conducted by Wood. Most parts are played by multiple performers. For the parts played by mulitple performers, they are indicated as follows:

Due to the controversial nature of the turkey trot (and sometimes of ragtime in general), he was being cautious about his identity and reputation by using a different name. description: In very brief, it's a piano educational story of Czeny's 299 Works-collection book and one of its pieces - No. 27. I found it's treble part containing a whole view of a scale from high pitches to bass ones, which was suitable for a boy's nutrition of vocal situation - from higher pitches to his growth to be a man - bass part. Meanwhile, hands' controllability of 4 parts can also be improved. Therefore, in classroom, I suggested myself and my boy students to train themselves in usage of this piece. I thought it's good for them. I think: partly to say, appreciating Vienna school's beauties, mean

Wo ist doch mein Freund geblieben?
Will Er mich denn nicht mehr lieben?
Er hat sich in dieser Nacht,
da ich aus dem Schlaf erwachte
und an seine Huld gedachte,
aus dem Bette weggemacht.
Ach ich habe den verloren,
den ich einzig mir erkoren!
Ach, ich habe nicht betrübt!
Er ist der, der mir gefallen,
darum soll mein Stimm erschallen:

Schönste(r), wo befindst du dich?
Soprano
Hör ich doch des Freundes Worte!
Ruft Er nicht an diesem Orte?
Soprano/Bass

title: File:Yokohama by Mollie King (1904).opus
description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/8418707?from=youtube_share 
Here's a really nice march two-step from a Canadian composer who published several pieces. The title and cover artwork are a puzzle, as there's nothing much I can see about the music that is very Japanese. The score as written ends too quickly so again I've taken the liberty of extending it by inserting a couple sets of repeat bars. Published by W.H. Scroggie in Montreal in 1904. The first of two nice pieces from this same composer.

Original score source was from Library and Archives

title: File:Ты каждый день меня пытаешь. Анастасия Вяльцева (IA 1901-gramophone-concert-records-g.-23111).flac
description:
Песня "Ты каждый день меня пытаешь", исполненная Анастасией Вяльцевой. Музыка Эрика Мейер-Гельмунда.
Слова песни:
Ты каждый день меня пытаешь
И всякий раз узнать желаешь:
Люблю ли я тебя, дитя?
Ужели ты не веришь?
Мою любовь и месяц знает.
Он счастья мне с тобой желает;
Поди, спроси ты у него,
Как искренно люблю я!
А если месяц не ответит,
Так могут звёзды рассказать:
Они подметили, наверно,
Как о тебе я всё мечтаю.
Мой друг, не спрашивай, люблю ли я!
Я повторю одно и то же:
Люблю тебя, ты жизнь моя,
Ты мне всего дороже!
Но нет, зачем искать на небе нам
Того, что сердце затаило,
Ты всё прочтёш
name: Ты каждый день меня пытаешь. Анастасия Вяльцева (IA 1901-gramophone-concert-records-g.-23111)
categories: Category:Audio files of songs in Russian

title: File:“Louisville” - California Ramblers (1923).opus
description:
California Ramblers put out hundreds of records under a smokescreen of pseudonyms across a wide spectrum of labels. But their primary label from late 1923 onward under the California Ramblers moniker was Columbia. 
While they recorded a few sides with Columbia in 1922, the relationship came to a head in the summer of 1923, when the Ramblers recorded five sessions for Columbia that resulted in seven sides that sold quite well - including this one, an energetic arrangement of Irving Caesar's "Louisville".
